posts.text: Why the Stay-Put Update exists: in 1.1.0 a few pop-ups still flashed open in a new tab for a moment before Undirect closed them. Closed or not, you'd seen the ad. 1.1.1 refuses them at the tap itself and shows the pop-up breaking like glass instead.

The bug that started the Stay-Put Update: in Undirect 1.1.0 a few pop-ups still opened in a new tab for a moment before Undirect shut them. You'd already seen the ad by then. So 1.1.1 refuses the pop-up at the tap, and the glass breaking is what you see in its place.

posts.day: Sat Nov 28 (Fri Nov 27 in the US)
posts.text: When Undirect stops a pop-up, the glass breaks from the exact spot your finger landed: rings and spokes round the tap, small pieces near it and big ones further out. The pane shows whole for 170 ms, hangs cracked for 120 ms, then falls, nearest pieces first. I wanted you to see that the page tried something and that it didn't work.

Safari gives extensions no way to send a notification, so when Undirect stops something it says so on the page itself: a small dark note at the bottom with the address the page tried to send you to. The address shows on red for half a second, then gets wiped off and stays struck through.

I built seven made-up websites that misbehave on purpose, so you can try Undirect without going near a sketchy page: a film site whose Play button fires a pop-up, a file host with an invisible layer over it, a news article that sends you away while you scroll, a sports stream that breaks the Back button. They can only reach a stand-in page that does nothing.
One part of the Stay-Put Update that's easy to miss: Undirect now runs on iPhone and iPad with iOS 18 too, so an iPhone that never got the newest iOS can use it.

If you'd rather not see the glass or the note, both switch off in Undirect's menu in Safari or in the app, and the gear on the note opens that menu. Undirect keeps stopping pop-ups either way; it just does it without a word.

Close up, the stone in the Stay-Put art has a pale vein through it, and the stack under it is squared by hand: every half-millimetre sheet sits a hair off the one below. Perfect shapes are what make a render look fake, so I wrote the flaws in on purpose.

The same picture twice. On the left, what the path tracer has after one light path per pixel; on the right, after 900, which is the finished art for the Stay-Put Update. Every grain on the left is one ray that found a light or didn't.
